speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To help me pinpoint the cause, could you please tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the progression from urinary incontinence over a year to significant gait difficulty and recent speech changes, do you notice any stiffness or tightness in your leg muscles, or is there any numbness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA).

The combination of progressive parkinsonism (rigidity, tremor), autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence), and bulbar symptoms (slurred speech) with a rapid decline over 3-4 months is highly characteristic of MSA. I will not order further tests as the clinical presentation is diagnostic.
